criticism: Reentrancy vulnerability exists when a function uses the delegatecall instruction, potentially having its own vulnerability.
This vulnerability occurs when the amount of Ether transferred is not checked, leading to potential loss of Ether due to malformed return statements.
This vulnerability exists when a contract relies on external code to transfer Ether without having its own functions to send Ether.
Arithmetic vulnerability occurs when the result of a division or arithmetic operation lies outside the range of the integer type, causing truncated values due to limitations in the EVM stack.
